en: The Amoghapāśahṛdaya-mantra Sūtra, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was on Mount Potalaka, contemplating himself...
Within the palace,
there were many precious sāla trees,
tamāla trees, and campaka trees.
There were aśoka trees and trees of supreme liberation;
furthermore, they were adorned all around by immeasurable varieties of jewel-trees,
with fragrant flowers and soft grasses found everywhere.
Furthermore, there are immeasurable jewel springs and ponds,
filled to the brim with water possessing the eight virtues,
adorned with various flowers that are most delightful to behold.
Furthermore, there are boundless varieties of birds and beasts,
their forms exquisite and wondrous, all endowed with hearts of compassion;
they produce various sounds that are ever like the performance of music.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of eight thousand bhikṣus,
ninety-nine koṭi-nayuta-hundred-thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devas from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens.
The host of Īśvara devas, the host of Maheśvara devas, Mahābrahmā, and other celestial hosts,
surrounded him before and behind by immeasurable hundreds of thousands, listening to the Buddha’s preaching of the Dharma.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the assembly named Avalokiteśvara.
He rose from his seat and adjusted his robes.
Baring one shoulder and placing his right knee upon the ground,
he joined his palms toward the Buddha;
with a serene and joyful countenance and a smile upon his face, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
I possess a divine mantra-heart called the Amoghapāśa.
In the past, during the ninety-first kalpa,
there was a world named Viśeṣadarśana.

In that place dwelt a Buddha named Lokendrarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Worthy One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, Bhagavān.
Out of compassion for me, that Buddha, the World-Honored One,
taught me this Great Divine Mantra Heart.
At that time, by virtue of my upholding it, its majestic spiritual power [was manifested].
He constantly [preaches] for the immeasurable hosts of the Śuddhāvāsa devas,
the hosts of the Īśvara devas, the hosts of Maheśvara devas, Mahābrahmā, and other celestial hosts.
I have transformed all those who have paid homage, made offerings, shown respect, and offered praise— numbering in the hundreds of thousands of immeasurables—
causing them to incline toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
It is by the power of such merit that I rely upon this.
He immediately attained the Great Samādhi of the Ten Billion Adornments of the Foremost Sublime Wisdom of Non-Voidness.
By the power of this concentration, he directly perceived the infinite and incalculable Buddha-worlds of the ten directions.
All the Tathāgatas and their assemblies all went to make offerings and listen to the True Dharma,
successively transforming and teaching immeasurable sentient beings.
They cause all beings to resolve their minds upon the unsurpassed enlightenment;
therefore, the power of this mantra is inconceivable,
capable of rescuing sentient beings from immeasurable suffering and calamity.
All those who possess wisdom should receive and uphold it.
World-Honored One, wherever else this heart-mantra exists,
one should know that such places have Īśvara, Maheśvara, Brahmā Devānām Indra, and others as their leaders.
Together with twelve billion hosts of devas,
they shall constantly protect, revere, and make offerings to it,
treating it as a shrine of the Buddha (buddha-caitya) so that no violence or evil may occur.
Various spirits and deities dwell and roam therein.
Wherever the World-Honored One travels through cities and villages,
he shall circulate this Heart Sūtra of the Amoghapāśa Divine Mantra in this manner.
It should be known that among these sentient beings,
they have already planted various roots of goodness under immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas,
and have come here by the power of their great vows.
World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who commit various grave offenses, practice evil dharmas,
insult and humiliate the worthy and holy ones, and slander the true Dharma.
They shall fall into the Avīci Great Hell,
where they will undergo various intense sufferings for incalculable kalpas.
[This applies to] all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas.
Although they possess supernormal powers, they are unable to save them.
If those beings hear this Heart Sūtra of Divine Mantras,
they will be able to give rise to remorse and shame, and will never again commit such acts.
If they can further observe the fast and precepts for one day and night, and recite this dhāraṇī-heart,
the karmic offenses they have committed will be experienced as light in their present life.
They shall no longer fall into the Avīci Hell.
How is it known that they will experience only light suffering in the present and not fall into hell?
It is said that even if they should suddenly encounter illnesses such as cold or heat, [they will not suffer].
It may last for one day, or two days,
or even up to seven days; or one may suffer from pain in the eyes,
pain in the ears, pain in the nose, pain in the teeth, pain in the gums, pain in the lips, or pain in the tongue.
Or there is pain in the gums and palate; or pain in the chest and heart;
or pain in the abdomen and navel; or pain in the waist and spine;
or pain in the ribs and armpits; or pain in the genitals and hips.
Or pain in the thighs and knees; or pain in the limbs and joints;
or pain in the hands and feet; or pain in the head and face;
or pain in the nape of the neck and the back of the head; or pain in the shoulders and upper arms.
They may suffer from wind-disorders, gas-disorders, hemorrhoids, dysentery, or leprosy;
or they may encounter chronic ailments, white leprosy, severe leprosy, and various scabies and eczema;
or they may contract pustules, sweet sores, flower-like sores, discharging sores, or poisonous sores.
Or they may encounter congestive swellings, wandering swellings, carbuncles, abscesses, or toxic swellings;
or suffer from epilepsy or chronic dampness;
or be afflicted by malevolent spirits or subjected to sorcery and curses.
Or being cursed with incantations, or being subjected to poison;
or being imprisoned, or being bound in shackles and manacles;
or being beaten and reviled, or being slandered.
Or they may be subjected to schemes of harm, or to intimidation,
or again encounter various other forms of disadvantageous events involving increase or decrease;
in short, all such things.

All physical and mental afflictions of oppression, as well as the seeing of evil dreams, are thereby proven to be light sufferings manifested in the present; they shall no longer lead to a fall into the Avīci Hell.
All committed karmic offenses shall be completely eliminated.
By the power of this mantra, even for such sentient beings,
heavy offenses are manifested as light sufferings and are thereby eradicated.
How much more so for other sentient beings whose bodies and minds are pure;
if they hear and uphold this mantra, they shall not fail to obtain blessings,
and their karmic offenses from previous lives shall likewise be eliminated.
They shall always experience happiness in the present and the future.
World-Honored One, if there should be members of the fourfold assembly or those of the four castes who,
out of a mind of flattery, crookedness, or deceit, [act in such a manner].
Having heard this Heart Sūtra of Divine Mantras,
one should receive, uphold, read, recite, copy, and make offerings to it; and for the sake of others,
one should praise and explain it, instructing them to hear and receive it.
He even went as far as to approach the ears of animals himself,
earnestly reciting so that they might hear it,
while further carefully contemplating the phrases and verses of this mantra.
Because it does not involve disparagement, because it does not grasp at signs,
because it is non-conceptual, because it is without origination,
because it is not slow in its activity, and because it is unconditioned.
Because it is free from defilement, because it is an impartial mind,
because it is without increase or decrease, and because it is free from the five aggregates,
one further cultivates the recollection of the Buddhas through this skillful means.
By the power of such merit,
ten Buddhas appear before him from each of the ten directions,
instructing him to repent and eliminate the sins he has previously committed.
May all aspirations be fulfilled.
Should one be unable to do as described above,
one may at least transcribe this Heart Sūtra of Divine Mantras.
If one places [this image] within one's home and pays homage and makes offerings to it,
one shall likewise obtain immeasurable and boundless merit.
World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings...
For the sake of overcoming others, or out of fear of a master;
out of fear of enemies, or fear of wild beasts;
out of fear of peril, or out of compliance with others.
Or, seeking high status and abundant wealth and treasures,
they may hear such a Heart Sūtra of Divine Mantras; yet,
although they have heard it, they do not treat it with reverence.
Furthermore, even if they should slander, despise, or revile [this teaching],
the wise should know that this is not due to their own power; rather,
it is through the majestic spiritual power of Avalokiteśvara that he causes them to hear it with their ears.
In order to bring about their benefit and happiness in the present and the future, the World-Honored One said:
"For example, suppose there were a person who gathered aloeswood, musk, or perhaps sandalwood and camphor."
Though they are subjected to various forms of slander, contempt, and revilement,
and are even ground down to be smeared upon their bodies,
the agallochum, musk, and other such substances do not form such thoughts.
Just as that [fragrance] despised me and did not give me its scent,
yet by its very nature it constantly performs the function of fragrance;
so too is this heart-mantra of the divine incantation.
Even if they encounter slander, contempt, or disparagement,
or as previously mentioned, write it down, receive and uphold it, and respectfully make offerings to it with a mind of flattery and deceit.
Furthermore, they act as the causes and conditions for those roots of goodness,
so that in whatever place they are born in the future,
they shall be endowed with the sublime fragrance of the merits of ethical discipline, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Furthermore, because it can also perform such fragrant deeds for others,
the majestic power of this divine mantra is inconceivable;
it is able to bring about beneficial results for both those who believe in it and those who slander it.
Blessed One, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family,
as well as bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs,
upāsakas, or upāsikās—

Or if other people, on the eighth day of the waxing moon, observe the fast and precepts and recite this Great Divine Heart-Mantra with single-minded devotion for as many as seven times without intermingling it with other speech.
It should be known that such a person will certainly obtain twenty benefits in the present life.
What are these twenty?
First, their body will be free from various ailments, remaining secure and happy.
Second, by the power of past karma, although illnesses may arise, they are swiftly cured;
third, the body is delicate and soft, the skin has a radiant luster, and the face and eyes are bright and clear.
Fourth, one is loved and respected by the multitude.
Fifth, one closely guards the sense faculties.
Sixth, one acquires abundant wealth and treasures to enjoy as one wishes.
Seventh, the wealth and treasures one acquires cannot be plundered or damaged by kings, thieves, water, or fire.
Eighth, all undertakings and activities will be successfully accomplished.
Ninth, all plantings will not be threatened by malevolent dragons, frost, hail, wind, or rain.
Tenth: If crops are afflicted by calamities or misfortunes, recite this mantra over ashes or water seven times.
Then, within the field, establish a boundary in the eight directions and sprinkle [the ashes or water] above and below.
At that time, all calamities and misfortunes will be immediately extinguished.
Eleventh, one shall not have one’s vital energy (*ojas*) sucked away by any violent and malevolent spirits, *rākṣasīs*, and the like.
Twelfth, all sentient beings who see or hear [this] will rejoice.
Thirteen: they always delight in and respect [the Dharma], never becoming weary or satisfied.
Fourteen: even if they encounter enemies or adversaries, these are swiftly and naturally extinguished.
Fifteenth, humans, non-humans, and others are unable to cause them harm.
Sixteenth, they are not affected by malevolent enchantments, curses, or sorcery.
Seventeenth, the entanglements and stains of the afflictions do not frequently manifest.
Eighteenth, swords, poisons, water, and fire cannot cause them harm.
Nineteenth, all devas and benevolent spirits constantly follow and protect them.
Twentieth, in every successive birth, they are never separated from loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
He attains these twenty benefits and further acquires eight qualities.
What are the eight?
First, at the time of death, one will see the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara appearing before them in the form of a bhikṣu, who will joyfully console and comfort them.
Second, they will pass away peacefully and without any suffering or pain.
Third, when about to relinquish life,
the eyes do not roll upward, the mouth does not gape open,
the hands cease their agitation, and the feet remain still without stretching or curling.
Fourth, when about to relinquish one's life,
one abides in right mindfulness, with no distracted thoughts.
Fifth, at the time of death, one does not die face-downward.
Sixth, at the time of passing away, one will attain inexhaustible eloquence.
Seventh, having passed away, one will be reborn in the pure lands of the Buddhas according to one's vows.
Eighth, one will never be separated from virtuous friends.
World-Honored One, if good sons and good daughters are able to abstain from alcohol,
meat, and various pungent spices,
and do not eat leftover or impure food, their bodies will remain constantly pure and clean.
If one recites this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra* three times every day,
those supreme merits will increase day and night. Furthermore,
if one can abandon the mind of stinginess regarding the Dharma and remain free from envy, [the merit will likewise increase].
Exclusively for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings,
one should observe whether those beings possess strength or lack it,
and then preach this Sūtra of Divine Mantras accordingly.
You should know that such individuals will swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
they shall enter the ranks of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
and it is for this reason that they are called "bodhisattvas."
"Bodhi" refers to prajñā;
"sattva" refers to upāya.
These two dharmas are thus.
He is able to bring about all benefit and happiness for all sentient beings.
World-Honored One, I now do this desiring to bring benefit and happiness to the fourfold assembly,
and to eliminate the sins committed by all evil sentient beings.
"Before the Tathāgata, I shall recite this divine mantra;
I pray that the World-Honored One will, out of compassion, grant his permission.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
The great assembly is pure and knows the proper time; you should speak.
I also rejoice in this.
This divine mantra-heart is the father and mother of bodhisattvas in future ages.
May the activities undertaken by all bodhisattvas be swiftly accomplished,
and may all things that cause fear be quickly extinguished.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Having received the Buddha’s permission, they were filled with joy and leaped for gladness;
gazing up at the Honored One’s countenance, they did not turn their eyes away for even a moment.
With palms joined in reverence, they addressed the Buddha, saying:
This divine mantra-heart is that which all bodhisattvas should revere, honor, and make offerings to;
it is the supreme dharma-gate for the perfection of liberation.
It brings benefit, welfare, and happiness to all sentient beings.
Those who wish to receive and uphold this heart-mantra should first pay homage to all Buddhas of the past, future, and present, as well as to all Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas.
Furthermore, one should pay homage to those who have attained the goal and practice correctly.
Furthermore, one should pay homage to the great śrāvakas such as Śāriputra and others.
Furthermore, one should pay homage to the great bodhisattvas such as the noble Maitreya and others.
Furthermore, one should pay homage to the Buddha Amitābha.
Furthermore, one should pay homage to the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.
Furthermore, one should pay homage to the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, who is endowed with great compassion.
Having performed this prostration, one should further reflect, saying:
"This heart-mantra of the divine spell is named Amoghapāśa;
it was [revealed] by the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara before the Tathāgata."
He personally expounded this amidst the great assembly.
I now recite it so that all my undertakings may be swiftly accomplished.
"May all things that cause me fear be swiftly extinguished.
Having formed this thought, one should recite:
*Tadyathā | aṃ | cchalo cchalo | jili jili | curu curu | Homage to the One Endowed with Great Compassion.*
Sara sara, siri siri, ciri ciri, niri niri; homage to the one with the great lotus hand.
Kara kara, kili kili, kulu kulu; homage to the greatly pure sentient being.
Bhavabhave, tathā tathā, kinni kinni; homage to the most pure sentient beings!
Kalakale, kirike kiri, kurulu kurulu; homage to the one who has attained great power!

Cchre lo cchre lo | saṃcchre lo saṃcchre lo | vicchre lo vicchre lo | iṭṭha iṭṭha | bala bala | bili bili | buru buru | ehi ehi | Homage to the Greatly Compassionate One who bears the form of the Great Beast King!
Daluo daluo, saluo saluo, sheluo sheluo, boluo boluo, heluo heluo, hehe xixi, huhu, wengjialuo; I prostrate to the Great Brahmā King’s form.
Daluo daluo, dili dili, dulü dulü, taluo taluo, saluo saluo, boluo boluo, baluo baluo. Homage to the one whose body is adorned with hundreds of thousands of lights.
Śivara śivara | Dabba dabba | Homage to the Blessed One, to the Sun, the Moon, Yama, Varuṇa, Agni, Vairocana, Śakra, and Brahmā.
He is worshipped by the hosts of celestial beings such as the Cāraṇas and others.
*Mala mala, mili mili, mulu mulu, suru suru, zuru zuru.* I prostrate to the boy Sana, Rudrāyudha, Viṣṇudatta, Siddhāyana, Yakṣa, and Kapilāyana, who possess many forms.

Dalō dalō, dilli dilli, duru duru, talō talō, jalō jalō, palō palō, dulō dulō, calō calō, halō halō, malō malō, balō balō. I prostrate to the One Who Grants Wishes, the Universal Observer, the Supreme Observer, the World-Sovereign, the Great Sovereign.
Muhu muhu | Mulu mulu | Muya muya | Muñca muñca | Lakṣa lakṣa | Homage to the one who is able to cause me and all sentient beings [to attain liberation].
Liberated from all fears, liberated from all malevolent sorcery,
liberated from all calamities and misfortunes,
and liberated from all diseases.
They are liberated from all malevolent spirits, demons, and goblins.
They are liberated from all enemies, killing, binding, threats, and beatings.
They are liberated from all calamities involving kings and calamities involving bandits.
May there be liberation from all calamities of water, fire, and wind;
may there be liberation from all calamities of weapons, poison, and the like.

*Kaṇakaṇa kiṇikiṇi kuṭukuṭu cchalo cchalo*. Homage to the one who is able to reveal all the faculties (*indriya*), powers (*bala*), factors of awakening (*bodhyaṅga*), factors of the path (*mārgāṅga*), and the Four Noble Truths (*catvāry āryasatyāni*).
Dhama dhama, sama sama, maha maha; I prostrate to the one capable of dispelling all great darkness, who has brought the six pāramitās to full growth and completion.
Mili mili, ṭaṭa ṭaṭa, thaṭha thaṭha, ḍhiḍhi ḍhiḍhi, śuśu śuśu. I bow my head to those who wear the amoghapāśa.
Endowed with great compassion, sovereign and most supreme,
you who are able to destroy all evil spirits and demons,
come quickly, come quickly, and protect us!
Kulu kulu, pala pala, sala sala, kala kala, kata kata, mata mata; I prostrate to the one who dwells in the Pure Land and possesses great compassion.
He wears white auspicious threads upon his body,
adorns his neck with necklaces of various jewels,
and crowns his head with a flower garland and a jeweled tiara.
Within the jeweled crown upon the crown of his head, there is an image of the Omniscient One,
holding a magnificent and rare jewel-lotus;
he is endowed with all the wondrous merits of the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), absorptions (*samādhi*), and liberations (*vimokṣa*).
They remain entirely unshaken;
they are skillfully able to bring all sentient beings to maturity and are endowed with great compassion.
It can eliminate all karmic obstructions,
rescue all from the suffering of illness,
and universally bring comfort to all sentient beings.

*Amṛtāyur-lakṣmī-vijaye oṃ mūka-prasāda-jayini amṛte svāhā | namo ’mogāya svāhā | namo ’rhatāya svāhā | namo ’pratihate svāhā | namo vairocanāya svāhā | namo sarva-karma-siddhyai svāhā | añjaye jñāne svāhā.* This heart-mantra of the deity, when recited, will certainly produce results.
Those who are able to receive and uphold this shall have all their desires fulfilled.
If one recites it one hundred and eight times each during the three periods of every day,
the five sins of immediate retribution will certainly be extinguished.
There is no karmic obstruction that will not be purified.
When one wishes to perform recitation, one should first establish a boundary.
As for the method of establishing this boundary:
Take either ashes, water, white mustard seeds, or a mountain-peg;
having recited the mantra seven times over them, drive them into the four directions.
Burn aloeswood incense and recite with a focused mind.
For those suffering from chills, fevers, or malaria, one should recite the mantra over a thread twenty-one times and tie it around the neck or arm;
thus they shall be cured. For those with other ailments, [one should apply] either clarified butter or oil.
Alternatively, one may recite a mantra over water twenty-one times and give it to them to drink, whereby they will immediately be cured.
This applies to those who wish to dispel the curses, incantations, and spells cast by others.
Take clay, flour, beeswax, or other materials to fashion an image of that being;
reciting this mantra while holding a sharp sword in hand,
sever it with deep compassion for that being.
Furthermore, by tying a mantra-thread around the body of one who is afflicted with loathing,
all fears shall be immediately dispelled and cured.
For those suffering from abdominal ailments, one should recite the mantra over salt water.
If one causes them to wear it, they will immediately be cured.
This applies to all those afflicted by *gūduka* poisons,
or those stung by snakes, scorpions, and the like.
One should consecrate water for them to drink and consecrate mud to smear upon them;
thus, all ailments and eye pains will be immediately cured.
One should also consecrate white thread and tie it upon their ears.
They shall immediately be cured.
For those who suffer from toothaches,
one should recite the mantra over twenty-one pieces of *karṇīra* wood.
By chewing and rubbing it [upon the body], one will immediately attain healing and recovery.
In all places of fear,
one should establish a boundary (sīmābandha) and dwell therein.
As for the method of establishing the boundary (*sīmābandha*):
recite the mantra over five-colored threads twenty-one times,
wrap them around the mountain-shoulder stakes, and drive them into the four corners.
One will immediately attain fearlessness.
Those who wish to protect themselves should wear a thread consecrated with mantras upon their bodies.
Alternatively, one may recite mantras over water and ashes and sprinkle them upon the body.
For those possessed by various ghosts or spirits,
one should commonly wear five-colored threads after consecrating them with mantras.
Even if one has abandoned [the remedy],
for all ailments such as sores and swellings,
take the powder of *pippalī* (long pepper), mix it with honey, and recite the mantra over it twenty-one times.
By applying it to the affected area, one will immediately achieve healing.
Those with eye ailments should consecrate scented water, licorice water, or *bhallātaka* water twenty-one times with mantras.
By using it for washing, one will immediately achieve recovery.
For various ailments of the ears and nose,
one should consecrate boiled oil twenty-one times with mantras.
If one drips [this medicine] into the ears and nose, it will immediately bring about healing and recovery.
For all those who are oppressed and distressed by various official matters, such as strife, contention, enmity, slander, and injustice;
One should consecrate pure water twenty-one times with mantras;
by washing the face and sprinkling it upon the body, one will immediately achieve reconciliation.
Whenever calamities arise in any kingdom, royal capital, city, or town, [one should act likewise].
One should consecrate the maṇḍala by smearing the ground with cow dung and sprinkling it everywhere with fragrant water;
at each of the four corners of the site, place a jar, and within those jars, place flowers and water.
Spread fresh, clean grass over the ground of the site.
Arrange fine fruits and foods upon it, and place flour-lamp bowls with pure wicks soaked in fragrant oil at the four corners and light them.
One should scatter various kinds of flowers throughout the site and offer worship by burning the finest incense.
As for the one who recites the mantra:
Having bathed in fragrant water and donned fresh, clean robes,
one should sit upon a pure seat with body upright and mindfulness established, reciting this heart-mantra.
If the practitioner is sincere, calamities and disasters will immediately cease.
In any place where there are epidemics, malevolent spirits, or calamities,
if one sprinkles water from a consecrated flask upon that location and one's own body,
all misfortunes and afflictions will be entirely extinguished.
If one is afflicted by malevolent spirits or enchantments,
grind sandalwood incense with water from a flask,
recite the mantra twenty-one times, and apply it to the heart center.
Demonic possession and bewitchment shall immediately cease.
If one constantly recites this divine mantra-heart,
all obstacles such as the four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, and the slandering of the Dharma will be entirely eliminated.
If one wishes to protect the state and its dwellings so that no calamities or misfortunes occur,
one should take one hundred and eight lotus flowers,
recite the mantra over each one once, and cast them into the fire altar.
By making offerings to the worthy and holy ones,
calamities and misfortunes will all cease, and the state and one's home will be peaceful and secure.
If one wishes to cause others to regard oneself with a heart of compassion, such that they no longer harbor resentment or jealousy, [one should do so].
One should take one hundred and eight pieces of sandalwood,
each two inches long, and recite the mantra over each once before casting them into the fire altar as an offering to the worthy sages and saints.
It can cause that person to feel compassion for oneself and harbor no resentment.
If one fears being afflicted by pestilence or malevolent spirits,
one should take śyāmāka and viśyāmaka herbs.
Nāṅguli medicine, Khaṇḍanāṅguli medicine,
Vārāṇī medicine, Oṃ-vajra-pāṇi medicine, Indrapāṇi medicine.
Gandhabbilyaññu-jaṭā, Kumbhāṇḍa-jaṭā, Yakṣa-jaṭā,
Mahāyakṣa-jaṭā, Viṣṇukrāntā-jaṭā.
The Somarasa medicine, the Sunanda medicine, the Jayanti medicine,
the white sandalwood medicine, the Śārima medicine, the Śāripa medicine,
the Khasitipavaraṇī medicine, and the Khāriśuka medicine.
The Gandhāra-kośa medicine, the Vajra medicine, the Kṛṣṇa medicine,
and the Vālāha-kṛtanta medicine— these various medicines should be finely pounded and sifted through silk.
Then, mixed with water, they should be formed into pills the size of jujube fruits.
If one recites this mantra one hundred and eight times and places it upon the crown of the head or ties it to both arms,
pestilence and malevolent spirits shall not afflict the body.
If there are young children who are terrified by demonic influences or malevolent ghosts, [this shall likewise protect them].
Recite this mantra over these medicinal pills one hundred and eight times.
If they are tied beneath the throat, one will no longer be terrified.

This is the Postscript to the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya-mantra-sūtra*. Regarding this *Amoghapāśahṛdaya-mantra-sūtra*:
This is indeed the aphorism of the knowledge of all modes throughout the three periods of time;
it is the ultimate destination for realizing truth on the ten stages.
It tears asunder the snare of the four māras.
They have broken down the evil banners of the six teachers,
set in motion the peaceful chariot for all disciples,
and proceeded along the level path to the site of enlightenment.

For this reason, the various kingdoms of India all call it the "wish-fulfilling divine pearl" (cintāmaṇi);

The titles such as "Amoghapaśa" and so forth are the specific designations of various sūtras. For instance,
it is like casting a lasso to capture a beast.
At times it may seek the void;
this teaching moves the drumhead so that nothing does not accord with the profound mystery.
Therefore, it receives this name.
That which reaches the ultimate limit of movement without fixed direction is called "spirit" (shen).
That which issues commands and warnings to all things is termed "incantation" (zhou).
That upon which names and forms depend is designated as "mind" (xin).
Although the vehicles unfold as one or five and the treasuries open as two or three,

Those who unfurl the silken cords of the Dharma-realm all take this principle as their standard and turn toward this teaching.
Therefore, a sutra says:
"This body is like a city, with the mind-king dwelling in its center.
Furthermore, when one reaches the ultimate merit, it is free from marks, most wondrous, and reaches the furthest reaches.
Because it resembles the mind, it should be designated as such.
Therefore, a sutra says:
"Just like the mental consciousness of sentient beings."
Although its substance exists, it lacks such characteristics as length, shortness, squareness,
or roundness; this is the center of all phenomena and the ultimate pinnacle of formlessness.

At that time, as the reign of the Bao-li era was newly established,
those who could transmit the master’s craft were few;
consequently, while the divine images to which people turned for refuge were present, the ritual protocols for their veneration had not yet been fully established.
Furthermore, the mantras and the physical forms were both preserved in their Sanskrit language;
consequently, those who received and upheld them grew weary from their labors,
as the mixture of elements remained entirely indistinct.
